claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To begin, I need to understand a bit about your child or children. 

**First, let me ask: How old is your child?** (If you have multiple children you'd like to ask about, we can check them one at a time)

The age matters because:
- Children **under 16** may automatically qualify
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age, and if you'd like, their name so I can keep track as we go through the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hi! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. 

I have one child - Alex, who's 17 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one child, Alex, who is 17 years old.

Since Alex is 17 (which falls in the 16-19 age range), their eligibility will depend on whether they're in approved education or training. Let me navigate to the next step.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to know about Alex's education or training situation:

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as full-time non-advanced education at school or college), OR
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last 20 weeks), OR
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave?

Could you let me know which situation applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is still in education - he's doing his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is doing A-levels at sixth form college, that's full-time non-advanced education, which can qualify. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels at sixth form college are considered **approved non-advanced education**. Now I need to verify a few details to ensure Alex's education qualifies:

1. **Is Alex studying full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)

2. **Is this education funded or arranged by an employer**, or does Alex have an agreement for a future job with an employer who's supporting the education?

3. **Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (If yes, there's an additional dependency requirement)

Could you answer these questions for me?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is studying full-time - it's a regular sixth form college course, nothing to do with any employer. And no, he's not married.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! That all checks out. A-levels at sixth form college, full-time, with no employer involvement, and Alex isn't married - this is approved education. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week?** (Or not in paid work at all?)

This is important because children aged 16+ who work 24 or more hours per week don't qualify for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, actually Alex does work quite a bit - he has a part-time job at the supermarket and works full-time hours there alongside his studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I need to clarify this to make sure I understand correctly:

**Does Alex work 24 hours per week or more at the supermarket?**

This is the specific threshold - if Alex works 24 or more hours per week, it could affect eligibility, even though he's still in full-time education.

Could you tell me approximately how many hours per week Alex works at the supermarket?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he does work 24 hours or more per week - it's quite a lot to balance with his studies, but he manages it.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me proceed with this information.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I've now completed the assessment for Alex. Let me provide you with the outcome:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

### Why Alex doesn't qualify:

Although Alex is 17 years old and in full-time approved education (A-levels at sixth form college), which would normally qualify, **the rule states that children aged 16 or over who work 24 or more hours per week are not eligible for Child Benefit** - even if they're still in approved education or training.

Since Alex works 24 or more hours per week at the supermarket, this makes him ineligible under the current rules.

### Important to note:

- **If Alex reduces his working hours to less than 24 hours per week** while continuing his A-levels, you would be able to claim Child Benefit again
- **Child Benefit can be reclaimed** if circumstances change - so if Alex's work situation changes, you can reapply

### What to do if Alex's situation changes:

If Alex reduces his work hours below 24 hours per week, you can make a new claim for Child Benefit. You can find more information at: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility

I understand this might be disappointing news, especially since Alex is managing both his studies and work. If you have any questions or if Alex's circumstances change in the future, please don't hesitate to reach out.
